COMPREHENSIVE TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION and PROJECT SCOPE********************************************The Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier facility requires a complex industrial electrical power generation, backup power, and automation and control system modernization project. This system is a critical component of the federal effort to prevent the movement of invasive aquatic species between the Great Lakes and Mississippi River basins. **********************Specifically, USACE needs to upgrade the backup generator and switchgear control systems at Permanent Barrier 1 (PB1) to correct unreliable operation caused by deficiencies in the original design, configuration, and wiring.  The project requires replacing generator controllers, modernizing breaker controls and communications, and rebuilding the control software and operator interfaces to improve reliable operation on utility and backup power. Work will require testing, operator training, and a phased changeover to maintain continuous barrier operations. Work will be performed at an active, mission-critical facility requiring careful coordination with ongoing operations, planned equipment outages, and system changeovers to maintain operational readiness and minimize disruptions. A critical requirement is the integration of new equipment into an active industrial facility while protecting existing operations. The anticipated work may include engineering, design review, equipment upgrades and replacement, control system programming, integration, testing, and commissioning of interconnected electrical and industrial automation systems. ******************************************************************TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES:******************************************************************The project requires specialized expertise in: a) generator synchronization and load management, b) switchgear automation, c) protective relaying, d) programmable logic controllers (PLCs), e) human-machine interfaces (HMIs), industrial communications, and associated monitoring and data management systems.**********************Contractors must possess the technical capabilities necessary to work with the existing systems and integrate new equipment while maintaining compatibility and functionality. The existing facility incorporates Rockwell Automation ControlLogix PLCs, FactoryTalk View SE, FactoryTalk Transaction Manager, Microsoft SQL Server, Basler generator synchronization and control equipment, Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) protective relays and RTAC equipment, and DEIF generator controllers.
